title: One rhapsody, piano and orchestra
work: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2, S. 244/2 — shared opening
question: What changes when Liszt’s opening gestures pass from Rachmaninoff’s piano to two orchestras?
intro: Rachmaninoff’s 1919 Edison side is the piano original; the 1936 Stokowski source credits Karl Müller-Berghaus’s orchestration, while Goehr’s 1945 source leaves the arranger unidentified. Only the shared opening is compared, using each recording’s first side without concatenation. Analysis shifts the orchestral pitch-class features by one semitone, not the playback audio; Goehr’s alignment has median confidence 0.788 and should be used with caution, not for precise tempo claims.
